entries.ready: text=3 issues in flight, 12 queued behind them.
entries.caption: Mission Control — live loops, the queue, the build farm and what needs you, at a glance.
entries.alt: The Ouroboros Mission Control dashboard for the Acme Robotics workspace, showing active loops, the queue and farm status.

entries.caption: One loop in the run console: its stage timeline, the agent's transcript and the changes so far.
entries.alt: The run console for a loop fixing a flaky CAN-bus telemetry test: the stage timeline with three stages done and Implementing on attempt 2 of 3, the agent transcript, and three changed files.

entries.caption: The sign-in page: continue with GitHub or your company's single sign-on.
entries.alt: The Ouroboros sign-in page, with the brand panel on the left and, on the right, Step 1 Sign in with Continue with GitHub and an enterprise SSO domain field, and a Step 2 preview of choosing where the loop runs.

entries.caption: The detection card: what Ouroboros found in the repository, with the evidence for each finding.
entries.alt: The We already figured this out card, listing the repository's language, build, devcontainer, tests, suggested protected paths and conventions.

entries.caption: Starting workflow templates — pick one, then edit it later in the Workflow Studio.
entries.alt: The Choose a starting workflow card with four template tiles: Quick fixes, Feature builder, Docs & chores and Deep refactor.

entries.caption: Your first issue: the safe one Ouroboros picked, with its estimate, and what keeps the first loop safe.
entries.alt: The Your first issue card showing the picked issue with its effort, workflow and estimated minutes, the buttons to pick another, and the safety list.

entries.caption: Smart defaults: what is already set up for you, and what you can add later.
entries.alt: The Smart defaults card, listing models through your own keys, builds on an enrolled runner, the nightly estimator and Slack after your first pull request.

entries.caption: What keeps the first loop safe: dry-run opens a draft pull request and never merges.
entries.alt: The safety list under the first issue: dry-run opens a draft PR and never merges, decisions wait in the Needs-you inbox, and auto-merge can be turned on in Settings, Policies.

entries.caption: A new workspace's dashboard offers the Get Started wizard until you run a first loop or dismiss it.
entries.alt: The Mission Control dashboard of a new workspace, with a banner reading New workspace — your first loop in about 4 minutes, and Get started and Dismiss buttons.

entries.caption: The app shell: the sidebar on the left, the header across the top, and the screen you are on in between.
entries.alt: The Ouroboros app on the Mission Control dashboard: the sidebar listing Dashboard to Insights with Needs You and Settings at its foot, and the header with the workspace chip, Search, the live-loop and Needs you pills, the bell and the account avatar.

entries.caption: The search palette: type to find a screen or a command, then press Enter.
entries.alt: The search palette open, with the Search screens and commands field, the Navigation group of Go to commands and the Actions group with Toggle theme and Sign out.

entries.caption: The account menu: font size, theme, workspace settings, keyboard shortcuts and sign out.
entries.alt: The account menu open under the avatar, showing your name and email, the Font size stepper, the Theme choices Light, Dark and System, and the Workspace settings, Keyboard shortcuts and Sign out items.

entries.caption: Issue intake: every open issue, sized before you ask, with its suggested workflow and model.
entries.alt: The Issues screen for Acme Robotics headed 9 open issues, 7 already sized, with Re-estimate all and Queue 0 selected buttons, a filter bar of repository, label chips, state, sort and search, and the backlog table showing each issue's effort chip and confidence, suggested workflow and routed model, beside an empty Issue detail panel.

entries.caption: An issue's sizing story: the estimate, its confidence and regression risk, and how it was produced.
entries.alt: The Issue detail panel for #484 Motor PID integral windup on wheel stall, marked sized, with its description, the AI work breakdown listing two files, about 150k tokens, a 10–16 minute cycle time, effort M at 88% confidence, medium regression risk with its reason, the standard-fix workflow and cursor/composer-2 model, the Queue for loop, Re-estimate and Open on GitHub buttons, and the estimation trace.

entries.caption: Three issues ticked: the selection bar totals their estimate and queues them under a workflow.
entries.alt: The backlog with #484, #489 and #487 ticked and, along the bottom, the selection bar reading 3 issues selected, est. 3h 40m combined autonomous work, with an Assign workflow menu button and a Queue → suggested button.

entries.caption: Planning: describe the work and draft tickets, with the trackers and the backlog's health beside it.
entries.alt: The Planning screen headed Describe the work. Ouroboros writes the tickets., with Import from Jira marked soon and New roadmap buttons; the Generate tickets card with its description box, structured outline, tracker choice of GitHub Issues, Jira and Linear, milestone select, the Auto-size with estimator and Queue XS/S tickets immediately switches and the Draft tickets button; and the Tracker sync and Backlog health cards.

entries.caption: A drafted batch under review: six tickets, sized and wired with dependencies. Nothing reaches the tracker until you push.
entries.alt: The Draft — 6 tickets list marked all sized: six ticked drafts OTA-1 to OTA-6, each with its title, the tickets it blocks, an effort chip, a suggested workflow and an Edit button, above the estimated total, Regenerate and Push 6 tickets to GitHub.

entries.caption: The roadmap: one lane per epic across the months, with progress and today's date.
entries.alt: The Roadmap — Helios 2.1 card, Q3 2026 to Q1 2027, with Share marked soon: a month grid from July 2026 to March 2027 with bars for OTA hardening (12 issues, 8 done), BLE provisioning v2 (9, 2), Motor control refactor (14, 0), Fleet telemetry dashboard (7, 0) and a dashed unscoped Zephyr 4.2 migration marked proposed, a TODAY line, and an Add epic button.

entries.caption: The push: one press writes every ticked draft to the tracker, blockers first.
entries.alt: The foot of a drafted batch: est. total ~3 days of loop time · $14 est. spend, a Regenerate button and the Push 6 tickets to GitHub button.

entries.caption: The Workflow Studio: every workflow in the rail, the selected one on the canvas, and the inspector beside it.
entries.alt: The Workflow Studio open on standard-fix, with Browse templates, Dry run and Publish v15 buttons, Visual, Code and Copilot (soon) tabs, a rail listing standard-fix, feature-loop, deps-refresh, docs-loop, hotfix-p0 (paused) and security-patch (not published) above + New workflow, the canvas with the first stages, and an empty inspector asking you to select a stage or an edge.

entries.caption: The standard-fix canvas: stages as cards, edges between them, and labelled branches and loops.
entries.alt: The whole standard-fix canvas at 50%: the trigger Issue queued, Understand & scope, the Effort re-check decision branching ≤ M to Write attack plan and > M to Split into subtasks and Back to queue, then Code the change, Build farm · pool A, Run test suite, Self-review diff and the Checks green? gate, which passes to Open PR & auto-merge or loops back on fail; the toolbar below holds zoom, Auto-layout, Add stage and Undo/Redo.

entries.caption: Select a stage and the inspector beside the canvas configures it — here the model stage Code the change.
entries.alt: The Workflow Studio with the Code the change stage selected: the inspector on the right shows its kind, Implement, its title and description, Mode set to Skill with zephyr-conventions, the prompt template with its variable palette, and the start of Model routing.

entries.caption: A field the inspector refuses: an empty prompt is marked, and the stage cannot be applied until it is fixed.
entries.alt: The Prompt template field of the Code the change stage, emptied and outlined, with Write the stage prompt. in red below it and the Insert a variable palette.

entries.caption: Publishing: the draft is checked, then frozen as the next version; runs queued from now on use it.
entries.alt: The Publish v15 dialog explaining that the draft is checked by both validators and frozen as the next version, that runs queued from now on use it and the draft stays open, with an optional Change note field and Publish v15 and Cancel buttons.

entries.caption: The code view: the same workflow as the canvas, as a typed file, with the explorer, the editor and the loop checks.
entries.alt: The Workflow Studio's Code tab open on standard-fix.loop.ts: the Explorer listing the workspace's workflow files, skills and the read-only ouroboros.config.ts; the editor showing the file's defineLoop call with its trigger and first stages, under the line Printed from the draft · Saves as you type.; and the Loop Checks, Types and Outline panel on the right, above the editor's status bar.

entries.caption: The Types card follows your cursor: here it documents route.alias, the call that pins a stage's model.
entries.alt: The panel beside the code editor: Loop Checks reading Graph acyclic except declared gate loop and 1 reference does not resolve; the Types card for the symbol under the cursor, route.alias(name: AliasName): ModelRoute, explaining that it pins the stage to one model registry alias; and the Outline of the twelve stages, with checks-green marked as the back-edge to 07.

entries.caption: A line the DSL cannot read: the save is refused, the place is marked, and the draft is left as it was.
entries.alt: The code workbench after a stage call was mistyped as lxlm: the word is underlined in red with a marker in the gutter, the line above the editor reads Not saved — this file does not parse yet. The draft is unchanged., and the strip below the editor counts 1 error with the message Line 15, column 5: lxlm is not a stage call, and lists the stage calls the DSL knows.

entries.caption: A live loop in the run console: the stage timeline, the agent's transcript, and the changes, resources and guardrails beside it.
entries.alt: The run console for Loop #1847, #482 Fix flaky CAN-bus telemetry test, marked as a simulated run: the header with its coding status, standard-fix v14, claude-fable-5, the elapsed time, the branch, a PR verification link and the Pause loop, Take over in IDE and Abort run controls; the stage timeline with Queued, Analyze and Plan done and Implementing on attempt 2/3 after an attempt failed its tests; the streaming agent transcript with tool, gate and model entries; and the Changes so far card listing three files and two commits.

entries.caption: A finished loop: merged, with its pull request linked, and no controls or steering left to offer.
entries.alt: The run console for Loop #1839, #474 Debounce e-stop interrupt handler: the merged status, standard-fix, claude-fable-5, a fixed elapsed time of 11m 00s and a PR #512 link; a stage timeline and a transcript with nothing recorded, the steer box closed because the run has ended; and the Changes so far, Resources and Guardrails cards.

entries.caption: A guardrail that failed: the diff touches a protected path, with the evidence beneath it.
entries.alt: The Guardrails card marked violations: Diff outside allowed paths has failed, with its evidence open — path boot/rollback_flag.c, rule protected-path, glob boot/**, and the detail that the path is protected by the workspace policy and needs a one-time allowance — above the line Policy: feature-loop · tenant acme-robotics.

entries.caption: The run header: the loop's status, workflow, model and branch, and the controls an owner or admin has over a live run.
entries.alt: The run header for Loop #1847, #482 Fix flaky CAN-bus telemetry test: the coding status, standard-fix v14, claude-fable-5, the elapsed time, the branch loop/482-canbus-flake with a copy button, a PR verification link, and the Pause loop, Take over in IDE and Abort run buttons.

entries.caption: The test results of one build: its attempts, the summary of what passed, failed and was flaky, and the suites it ran.
entries.alt: The Test results page for Run #1847, Build 3, of #482 Fix flaky CAN-bus telemetry test: standard-fix v14, 61/63 passed and still running, rig helios-rig-02 and PR #514; the Re-run failed (1), Re-run full suite and Send failures back to loop buttons with the note that no farm build produced Build 3; the Build attempts strip from Build 1 (49/63, 14 failed) to Build 4 (63/63, all passed) and the Next card; the partial note; the summary of 63 total tests, 61 passed, 1 failed (overshoot_under_load, HIL), 1 flaky (passed on retry 2/3, quarantine watching) and a wall time of 6m 12s; and the first suites.

entries.caption: A real failure: a hardware-in-the-loop measurement past its limit, with the log the test wrote.
entries.alt: The Failure detail card for Build 3, showing 1 of 1: the test path tests/hil/test_estop_release.py::overshoot_under_load, its log of three rig trials peaking at 2.1%, 2.4% and 2.3% overshoot and the assertion max overshoot 2.4% > limit 2.0%, and a Triage section saying no heuristic rule fired, above the slot where AI triage will appear once a provider is connected.

entries.caption: A flaky case in Mark & Route: the rule that pre-selected Flake — retry, and what pressing the button will do.
entries.alt: The Mark & Route card for ring buffer drains under burst: the four classes Product bug, Test needs update, Flake — retry and Infra — rig issue, with Flake — retry pre-selected and marked heuristic · passed on a sanctioned retry; an empty Correction note to the loop marked optional; the Block PR #514 until green and Auto re-run physical suite after fix toggles, both on; and the Mark as flake & re-run the case and Waive & annotate PR buttons.
